newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RESULTS TODAY-UNITS UP REMGRO, TOBACCO NAGS.
newsitem.headline: RESULTS TODAY-UNITS UP REMGRO, TOBACCO NAGS.

text.p: South African diversified industrial firm the Rembrandt Group Ltd (Remgro) is seen posting a robust 25 percent rise in year earnings buoyed by a strong contribution from subsidiaries and a depreciation in the rand.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings for the year to March 31 rising to between 327 cents and 380 cents, with consensus at 355.7 cents from 283.9 cents a year ago.
Remgro in February declared a dividend of 76.84 cents for the 12 month period compared with 62.45 the previous year.

But the group, whose mainstay earner is tobacco, is seen making provision for possible legal challenges after U.S. cigarette group Ligget admitted that smoking was addictive and damaging to health, analysts said.
"They will make provisions for any health claims in their results," said one analyst who asked not to be identified.

Ligget in April released to U.S. states suing the tobbaco industry sensitive documents on the harms of smoking. Their admissions are expected to have far-reaching legal effects and repercussions for tobacco companies worldwide.

But Remgro's possible worries about the consequences of Ligget's move would be offset by good performances from a number of its interests, analysts said. They singled out Vodacom, a mobile telephone service provider, Remgro's liquor interests and mining house Gencor Ltd .

"Vodacom is turning into profit, Gencor's results were good and tobacco is doing reasonably well because of the depreciation of the rand," an analyst said, adding that profits from Stellenbosch Farmers Winery Ltd and Distillers Corp Ltd would also help.
